flags: No road-building or byway-campaign history is supplied. The historical paragraph instead gives the documented change from Baca Ranch to national preserve.

FHWA lists 163 miles, while material maps 129.2 miles. The overview attributes the federal figure and describes the documented NM 4 drive; the tourism page’s broad loop description does not establish precise connecting roads through Cuba and Fenton Lake.

Cabezon is retained as a separate excursion and placed before the NM 4 moments, using its southern location in relation to Cañon and Jemez Springs. Material strip miles are not a continuous NM 4 itinerary.

Dropped Cabezon’s Navajo giant-and-twins account because only Wikipedia supplies it; no Navajo cultural source is cached. Tribal histories at Jemez are also supported only by Wikipedia, with its name forms retained.

Removed the bathhouse and Manhattan Project selection aside to keep the overview focused; both have cache support. No current reservation or access rules inferred from the tourism page’s undated language.
